fr.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
fr.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
fr.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
fr.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
fr.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
fr.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
fr.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
fr.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
fr.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
fr.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
fr.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
fr.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
fr.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

es.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
es.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
es.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
es.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
es.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
es.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
es.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
es.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
es.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
es.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
es.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
es.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
es.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

pt.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
pt.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
pt.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
pt.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
pt.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
pt.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
pt.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
pt.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
pt.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
pt.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
pt.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
pt.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
pt.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

de.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
de.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
de.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
de.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
de.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
de.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
de.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
de.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
de.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
de.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
de.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
de.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
de.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

it.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
it.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
it.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
it.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
it.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
it.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
it.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
it.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
it.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
it.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
it.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
it.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
it.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

uk.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
uk.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
uk.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
uk.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
uk.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
uk.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
uk.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
uk.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
uk.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
uk.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
uk.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
uk.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
uk.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

pl.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
pl.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
pl.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
pl.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
pl.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
pl.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
pl.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
pl.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
pl.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
pl.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
pl.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
pl.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
pl.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

tr.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
tr.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
tr.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
tr.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
tr.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
tr.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
tr.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
tr.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
tr.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
tr.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
tr.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
tr.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
tr.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

ar.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
ar.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
ar.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
ar.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
ar.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
ar.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
ar.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
ar.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
ar.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
ar.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
ar.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
ar.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
ar.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

hi.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
hi.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
hi.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
hi.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
hi.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
hi.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
hi.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
hi.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
hi.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
hi.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
hi.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
hi.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
hi.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

zh.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
zh.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
zh.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
zh.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
zh.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
zh.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
zh.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
zh.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
zh.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
zh.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
zh.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
zh.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
zh.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

ja.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
ja.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
ja.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
ja.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
ja.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
ja.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
ja.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
ja.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
ja.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
ja.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
ja.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
ja.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
ja.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

tl.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
tl.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
tl.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
tl.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
tl.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
tl.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
tl.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
tl.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
tl.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
tl.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
tl.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
tl.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
tl.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

sw.int.help.twilio_sms:
Uses your company’s own Twilio account. In the Twilio console copy the Account SID and Auth token, and use a phone number you own as From (+1…).
Recipients: fixed numbers and/or contact groups. Broadcasts to contact groups also go out here.
Replies: turn on incoming messages, save, then paste the address shown into your number’s “A message comes in” webhook (HTTP POST). Replying OK acknowledges the latest broadcast.
sw.int.help.twilio_whatsapp:
WhatsApp through your Twilio account: your WhatsApp-enabled Twilio number as From (or the Twilio sandbox number for testing).
WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages to people who wrote to that number in the last 24 hours; outside that window Meta requires approved message templates.
Replies come back the same way as SMS (paste the address into the WhatsApp sender’s incoming-message webhook).
sw.int.help.resend: Email through Resend (resend.com): an API key, and a From address on a domain you verified in Resend.
sw.int.help.sendgrid: Email through SendGrid: an API key with Mail Send permission, and a verified sender address as From.
sw.int.help.teams: In the Teams channel: ⋯ → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”. Finish the workflow and paste the URL it gives you.
sw.int.help.slack: Create an incoming webhook for the Slack channel (api.slack.com → your app → Incoming Webhooks) and paste its URL.
sw.int.help.discord: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
sw.int.help.google_chat: In the Google Chat space: Apps & integrations → Webhooks → Add webhook, then paste the URL (Google Workspace accounts).
sw.int.help.telegram:
Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token. Add the bot to your Telegram group and enter the group’s chat ID (it starts with -100…).
With incoming messages on, “Send a test” also links the bot, so what people write in the group comes into Watchtower. For that, turn off the bot’s privacy mode in @BotFather (/setprivacy) or make it a group admin.
sw.int.help.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: a service → Integrations → Events API v2 → copy the Integration key. Critical alerts and emergency broadcasts then page whoever is on call.
sw.int.help.radio:
For a radio or dispatch gateway that can send and receive HTTP (RoIP gateways, LMR/P25 bridges, CAD systems).
Out: Watchtower POSTs JSON (event, title, text, severity, data) to the URL you give, signed with X-Watchtower-Signature when you set a signing secret.
In: the gateway POSTs {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key. What happens on the radio side — text-to-speech on a talkgroup, a CAD incident — is set up in the gateway itself.
sw.int.help.webhook:
For anything that speaks HTTP: Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate, your own servers.
Out: a JSON POST to your URL for each item it is set to send (event, title, text, severity, data), signed with X-Watchtower-Signature: sha256=<HMAC of the body> when you set a signing secret; optional extra header for API keys.
In: POST {"text","from","lat","lng"} to the inbound address with the key in the x-watchtower-key header.
sw.int.help.cap: Publishes your broadcasts as a CAP 1.2 (Common Alerting Protocol) Atom feed — the format public alerting and many emergency systems read. Give the feed address to the partners who need it; it contains its own key.

sw.sig.d.good: Messages and alerts go through right away.
sw.sig.d.fair: Working, but slower — messages may take a few seconds.
sw.sig.d.poor: Weak link — some requests fail. Short messages work best; entries queue and retry.
sw.sig.d.offline: No connection to Watchtower. Field Log entries queue and send when signal returns; where you lose signal is recorded for the coverage map.
sw.sig.d.lost: This device has not reported for 10+ minutes.
sw.sig.note: Measured by Watchtower: real round trips to the server. Signal bars (dBm) need the native Android app.
sw.sig.noneTracked: No tracked members in the last 24 hours.
sw.sig.boardNote: From each member’s position reports (every ~15 s while Watchtower is open). Lost contact = no report for 10+ min. Tactical map → Signal shows the coverage history.
